# Rollout Plan: Migration of 40,000 Users from Legacy Billing to New Billing System

## Overview
Both systems will run in parallel throughout the migration. Users are migrated in phases based on read/write cutover to the new system, with the legacy system kept live and untouched as a fallback until well after 100% of users are migrated and stable.

---

## Phase 1: Pilot (2% of users — ~800 users)
**Entry criterion:** New billing system has passed end-to-end reconciliation testing against a shadow copy of production data for 14 consecutive days with zero unresolved discrepancies, and rollback tooling (re-pointing a user back to the legacy system) has been tested successfully in staging.

**Scope:** Internal accounts, employee accounts, and opted-in low-risk external customers (e.g., monthly invoice total under $50, no active disputes).

**Duration:** 2 weeks minimum.

---

## Phase 2: Early Majority (25% of users — ~10,000 users)
**Entry criterion:** Phase 1 completes its full duration with the billing-discrepancy rate below 0.1% of transactions, zero critical (Sev-1) incidents, and support ticket volume for billing issues no more than 10% above baseline.

**Scope:** Randomly sampled across customer segments and plan tiers, excluding enterprise/contractual accounts with custom billing terms.

**Duration:** 3–4 weeks, migrated in weekly sub-batches of ~2,500 users to preserve the ability to pause between batches.

---

## Phase 3: General Availability (63% of users — remaining ~25,200 users, including enterprise accounts)
**Entry criterion:** Phase 2 sustains the same health thresholds as Phase 1 (see halt metric below) for 2 consecutive weeks, finance has signed off on revenue reconciliation totals matching between old and new systems within 0.05%, and enterprise account managers have completed customer-specific billing term validation for their accounts.

**Scope:** All remaining users, including enterprise and custom-contract accounts, migrated in batches of no more than 5,000/week.

**Duration:** 4–5 weeks.

---

## Post-Migration Stabilization Phase (0% new migrations — parallel-run continuation)
**Entry criterion:** 100% of users migrated and Phase 3 health metrics hold steady for 30 consecutive days.

This phase runs the legacy system in **read-only parallel mode** for a minimum 60-day burn-in period for audit, dispute resolution, and regulatory reconciliation before any discussion of legacy system decommissioning — which is explicitly out of scope for this rollout plan and must be a separate, later initiative.

---

## Halt Metrics

- **Automatic halt:** If the billing-discrepancy rate (mismatched charges, duplicate charges, or missed invoices) exceeds **0.5% of transactions** in any rolling 24-hour window during any phase, pause all new migrations immediately and freeze the current batch until root-caused.
- **Automatic halt:** If payment failure rate for migrated users exceeds **2x the legacy system's 30-day baseline failure rate**, pause the rollout.
- **Automatic halt:** If Sev-1 incidents (billing outage, incorrect charge >$100, data loss) occur more than **1 time per week** during any phase, pause and convene an incident review before resuming.

---

## Risks

RISK: Duplicate charges occur when both systems attempt to bill the same user during the parallel-run window | Implement a distributed lock/source-of-truth flag per account so only one system is authoritative for billing at any time | Billing Platform Engineering Lead
RISK: Data drift between old and new systems causes reconciliation mismatches (e.g., payment method updates not synced) | Run automated bidirectional reconciliation jobs every 4 hours with alerting on any mismatch above threshold | Data Integrity/Reconciliation Team Lead
RISK: Enterprise customers with custom contract terms are migrated incorrectly, causing invoicing disputes | Require manual sign-off from account managers per enterprise account before inclusion in Phase 3 | Enterprise Account Management Lead
RISK: Rollback of a migrated user back to the legacy system fails or causes further data corruption | Test and rehearse rollback procedure for each phase in staging before that phase begins, and cap batch sizes so rollback scope stays small | Site Reliability Engineering (SRE) Lead
RISK: Customer support is overwhelmed by billing-related tickets during migration | Pre-train support staff on new system behavior and staff up support capacity by 20% during Phases 2 and 3 | Customer Support Operations Manager

PHASES: 3
